name: Lithium
occurrence: Found in igneous rocks and brine deposits (spodumene, petalite); never occurs free due to reactivity.
biologicalRelevance: Prescribed in controlled doses as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder — one of very few Group 1 metals with an actual pharmaceutical role.
notableCharacteristics: Least dense metal and the lightest solid element.
ncertRelevance: anomalous behaviour of lithium (diagonal relationship with magnesium)
whyHere: A single lone electron in the 2s orbital, far from the nucleus, is easy to lose — hence the +1 ion and classic Group 1 reactivity, though its small size makes it noticeably less reactive than sodium or potassium.
didYouKnow: Lithium's small ionic size gives it a 'diagonal relationship' with magnesium, so it behaves more like Group 2 in several reactions than like its own group.
genZNote: Group 1's quiet overachiever. Powers your phone by day, someone's mood stability by prescription.
